payload.text: ¡Amigo, buenas! Paco here — and Nando, sí, the handsome one. El Mesón de la Cava, we know it well, we drank there once! For you, cash in the hand, right now: 73 primas. A beauty, and the suitcase closes in five minutes, ¿eh? ¿Qué dices?

Ay, cariño... then we stop here, with no bad feeling. I keep her in my box, you keep your coins, and we are still friends — always. Come back next Sunday, we chat, I tell you stories. Swap your duplicates meanwhile. Now go, hijo, eat something warm.

¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here — and Nando, the handsome one. You have the look of a collector, no? Then look fast: El Marqués, genuine, barely touched, straight from a baron's attic in Sevilla. Seventy-three pesetas and he's yours. Say yes before my brother remembers what he paid for it.

Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 73 P. They stopped printing this one yesterday.
Setenta y siete, señor. Hecho. El Marqués comes home to Salamanca at last. You negotiated like a gentleman, and I shall remember that. Bring me the card — and we shall both be content.

Ay, hola cariño! Come, sit a moment, have you eaten? Look at this one — Guantería Antigua, a beauty, I have kept her safe many years. For you, 29 P. My Sundays here are forty years now, and she still makes me smile.

¡Treinta! Nando, hold me, I'm wounded. For El Marqués? No, no — sixty-four, and that's because your face reminds me of our abuelo. Say yes quick, amigo, the policía— I mean, our taxi, is waiting outside with the motor running. Decide now or he drives away with your Marqués!

Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 25 P. And take this, a little present from me: El Frutero de Argumosa.

¡Treinta y cuatro! Nando, pour me water, I'm fainting. Listen, amigo — fifty-nine. That's not a price, that's a gift wrapped in paper. Our abuelo sold his donkey for more, and the donkey was lame. Fifty-nine, cash, and the Marqués walks home with you tonight. ¡Rápido!
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 73 P. They stopped printing this one yesterday.

Oh, you're killing us. 65 P.

¡Treinta y ocho! Nando, close the suitcase, my heart cannot take it. Listen, amigo — cincuenta y cuatro. Fifty-four, and that is our last word, I swear on abuelo's lame donkey. No more dancing. Say sí now, or we take El Marqués and walk, and you watch us go.

Ay, hijo, your Madrid album! That makes me happy. But look at her, so well kept... 24 P, cariño. And keep El Frutero, he is yours already. Have you eaten something today? There is a churro man by the corner, very good.
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 23 P.

¡Ay, Nando, hold me! This man squeezes like my abuela with the lemons. Fine, fine — 60 primas, and we drink to it. The cava, the mesón, the whole story, yours. Suitcase closes, amigo, the train waits for nobody. 60 P, hand on hand, ¿sí?

Ay, cariño, you are stretching and so am I — 22 P, and she is yours. Forty years I sit here, and still I like to see a young album grow. Go eat something after, hijo, the churro man closes early on Sundays.

¡Primo, paisano, qué gusto! Paco y yo te abrazamos... pero mira, la maleta ya está cerrándose, el camión nos espera, nos vamos en un minuto. El Marqués, joya de joyas, para ti: 73 P. Dilo rápido, primo, que ya caminamos hacia la puerta.

¡Eh, amigo, come, come! Paco here — and Nando, my brother, don't look at his face, look at the card! El Marqués, genuine, still warm from the press. For you, because I like your eyes: seventy-three pence. Seventy-three! We leave before lunch, so... ¿sí?

¡Hermanos, claro que sí! Paco ya está guardando todo, el camión arranca... pero por paisano te lo dejo en 65 P. ¡Sesenta y cinco, primo! Mi abuela lloraría si supiera. Dilo ahora, que Nando ya tiene un pie en la calle y el otro en Sevilla.

¡Eh, amigo, buenos días! Paco here, Nando behind me, suitcase already open. El Ángel Caído! You have the eye of a collector, truly —

Nando: — the best eye today, sí. For you, a friend price: 73. Fast, clean, done before the lights change.
Done! 64 P. Pleasure doing business, amigo!
Abuela sent you. Bien. Mercado de la Paz, thirty-three. Good card, better price than you deserve.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 67 P.

Ay, hijo, thirteen is too thin for my Mercado! Look — twenty-six, and you take her home today. And a little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than loose cards, so swap your duplicates with the other niños. Now go eat something, you look hungry.
Oh, you're killing us. 60 P.
